title: Marquette and Jolliet down the Mississippi, 1673
summary: Marquette and Jolliet, with five voyageurs in two canoes, set out from Michilimackinac, crossed Wisconsin by the Fox and Wisconsin rivers, and entered the Mississippi on 17 June. They went down as far as the Quapaw villages on the Arkansas, learned that the river ran to the Gulf, not the Pacific, and turned back; they returned by the Illinois and the Chicago portage.

events.label: Onto the Mississippi
events.text: Marquette wrote that they entered the great river with a joy he could not express.

events.label: The Quapaw, and the turn back
events.text: The Quapaw (Akamsea) received them, and some had European goods and spoke of the Spanish further down. Convinced the river ran to the Gulf of Mexico and not the Pacific, and afraid of Spaniards, they turned back.
